title: Human-Computer Interaction: Model-View-Controller (MVC) Pattern
summary: Model–View–Controller (MVC) is a design pattern in Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) and software design that divides a system into Model, View, and Controller components to make programs easier to build, understand, and fix.

sections.title: Overview of Model–View–Controller (MVC)
paragraphs: Model–View–Controller (MVC) is a design pattern in Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) and software design.
It divides a system into three parts:
Purpose: To make programs easier to build, understand, and fix.
list: Model – the brain (data & logic)
View – the face (what you see)
Controller – the hands (what you do)

sections.title: MVC Restaurant Analogy
paragraphs: Think of MVC like a restaurant:
list: Model = kitchen (where the food is prepared = data/logic)
View = menu + food served (what the customer sees)
Controller = waiter (takes your order and delivers it between kitchen and you)

sections.title: 1. Model (The Brain of the System)
paragraphs: Stores and manages the system’s data and rules.
list: Knows everything about the system’s content.
Updates data when something changes.
Does not care about how things look on screen.
Without the Model, the program has no knowledge to show.

sections.title: 2. View (The Face of the System)
paragraphs: The visual representation of the data.
list: Shows information to the user in a friendly way.
Changes automatically when the Model updates.
Without the View, users can’t see or interact with the data.

sections.title: 3. Controller (The Hands of the System)
paragraphs: Acts as a bridge between the user and the system.
list: Takes input from the user (clicks, taps, voice, typing).
Decides what action to perform.
Tells the Model or View what to do.
Without the Controller, the user cannot communicate with the system.

sections.title: How MVC Works Together (Flow)
list: 1. User does something (click, tap, type) -> handled by Controller.
2. Controller updates the Model (changes data).
3. Model notifies the View of changes.
4. View shows the updated information to the User.

sections.title: Benefits of MVC
list: Separation of roles: Each part has its own job.
Easy to maintain: Designers can work on View, programmers on Model.
Reusability: One Model can work with different Views.
Flexibility: Changes in one part don’t break the others.

sections.title: Quick Analogy Recap
paragraphs: Remember: MVC is like teamwork. Each part has its own responsibility, and together they make the system run smoothly.
list: Restaurant: Kitchen (Model), Waiter (Controller), Served food (View).
Human body: Brain (Model), Hands (Controller), Face (View).
Music app: Song data (Model), Playlist screen (View), Play button (Controller).
